title: Assistive labeling and focus paths wiresketch notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the console component library review that focuses on assistive labeling, focus path semantics, and lightweight wire sketches for compact density UIs. Goal is to capture unresolved accessibility tradeoffs and surface a prioritized backlog for the next sprint (UX + engineering).

High level decisions to land: 
- Ensure form controls and list items have reliable programmatic labels even when visually condensed or collapsed.
- Define a canonical focus order for interleaved controls (main action, secondary actions, contextual menu) to avoid focus traps.
- Agree on live region usage for async status updates in the tasks table and job detail panes.

Problem statements and observed issues: 
1) Condensed rows in dense lists drop visible labels to save space, relying on icons only. Screen reader users lose context because icons lack descriptive accessible names.
2) Inline action buttons (edit, copy, retry) are visually grouped but in DOM are separated which makes tabbing jump unpredictably.
3) Flyout and panel open animations shift focus without moving it programmatically; some users land in the middle of interactive content instead of the heading.
4) Status updates (e.g. job queued -> running -> failed) are sent via toast only; the jobs table row does not notify assistive tech reliably.

Proposed rules (short):
- Never render an icon-only interactive control without an aria-label or aria-labelledby. Prefer visible label when space allows; otherwise add longform aria-label combined with role="button".
- DOM order must reflect logical tab order; no visually re-ordered items that break sequential keyboard flow unless role="presentation" is used intentionally with documented exceptions.
- When opening a panel/flyout, set focus to the panel heading (tabindex=-1 and .focus()) and add aria-modal if it blocks background content. Close should return focus to the invoking control.
- For status changes in list rows, use aria-live="polite" region inside each row (or a single focused region) so row-level updates are announced. For critical failures use assertive live instead.

Wire sketches and focus path examples (text sketches):
- Dense task row (visual): [checkbox] | [icon status] | NAME (truncated) | actions (••• menu) | inline buttons (retry)
  DOM order suggestion: checkbox -> name link -> inline buttons -> actions menu -> status icon (status announced via hidden aria-live)
  Rationale: Keep primary actionable link early; group destructive/secondary controls after primary. Screen readers will encounter the name before exposed action set.

- Modal/panel open flow:
  Trigger: keyboard -> Enter on "View details" -> JS opens panel -> JS focus(panelHeading) -> CSS animation runs (should not steal focus) -> keyboard: Tab -> first interactive control inside panel
  Notes: add focus-visible ring on heading while animation plays. If panel contains long form, add "skip to content" link inside panel that becomes first tab stop.

Accessibility checklist (practical):
- [ ] All icon-only buttons have aria-labels and title attributes for tooltip parity.
- [ ] All list row primary name elements are links or buttons with clear visible text; avoid using only title attributes as the only label.
- [ ] Keyboard-only navigation flows tested for each compound component (table row, card, accordion). Document expected tab sequences in component README.
- [ ] Add unit tests that assert focus order and presence of aria attributes (jest + axe snapshots).
- [ ] Live region pattern for row updates implemented and audited with VoiceOver and NVDA.

Edge cases and micro-interactions: 
- Drag handles: if rows are draggable, provide an alternative keyboard reorder UI and ensure draghandle has aria-grabbed toggle state or role="button" with pressed state.
- Overflow menus: if overflow menu is visually attached to a row, prefer rendering the menu DOM as sibling to the row (not portal to body) unless focus management is explicit. If portal needed, include aria-controls and aria-expanded on triggering button.
- Focus loss on fast animations: for quick open/close UX we should debounce focus management so assistive tech has stable targets.

Backlog (prioritized):
- P0: Convert icons-only cells in dense lists to include accessible names (JIRA-UI-987). Owner: Marco.
- P0: Implement panel-focus canonical helper in component library (focusTrap-lite, focus-to-heading). Owner: Ling.
- P1: Row-level aria-live pattern experiment and audit across hosted jobs and dedicated capacity tables. Owner: Aisha.
- P1: Document tab order rules in component READMEs and add automated tests. Owner: Samira.
- P2: Keyboard reorder API for draggable lists (design + eng spike).

Design notes and alternatives considered: 
- Alternative A: Keep icon-only UI for density, but add offscreen text for screen readers. Pros: minimal visual change. Cons: offscreen text can cause layout regressions if not handled correctly and increases DOM noise.
- Alternative B: Use abbreviation + tooltip mapping (e.g. S=staged, R=running). Pros: very compact. Cons: not accessible unless tooltips are keyboard-visible and have aria-describedby mappings.

QA plan and acceptance criteria: 
- Acceptance: All primary flows navigable with keyboard only and announcements made for row state changes. Axe score should not report critical contrast or label failures for updated components.
- Manual QA steps: 1) NVDA on Windows: navigate dense table via Tab + Arrow keys and verify announcements; 2) Mac VoiceOver: test rotor behavior on rows and headings; 3) Mobile TalkBack spot-check on compact list page.

Notes to implementers: 
- Small helper utility idea: ariaLabelForIcon(iconName, { contextName }) that returns localized long label and optionally appends "in row: <item name>" for extra clarity. Keep function small and local to DS.
- Add a storybook health-check addon that renders each compound component with keyboard focus trail overlay for designers.

Open questions: 
- Do we prefer per-row aria-live spans or a single global region for all list updates? Performance vs verbosity tradeoffs.
- How to handle focus when a row is updated and its content reflows (e.g., name becomes two-line)? Should we maintain scroll position or prefer programmatic scroll to keep focused element visible?

Next steps: 
- Sync with engineering (Marco, Ling) Feb 17 to align on API for focus helpers and aria utilities.
- Create JIRA tasks for P0 items and attach unit-test expectations to each.
- Prototype one dense table with aria-live per row and test with NVDA by Feb 24.

References and learning resources: 
- WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: listbox, combobox, and dialog patterns (link in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Internal console style tokens doc (see linked artifact).

Quick sketch (ASCII) - keyboard path example for dense row: 
  [Tab] -> checkbox 
  [Tab] -> NAME link (focus-visible) 
  [Tab] -> primary inline button (retry) 
  [Tab] -> overflow menu (aria-expanded=false) 
  [Enter] -> open overflow (focus first menu item) 

End of notes. This doc is a working draft; please add comments inline or update the 'Backlog' list with new owners/ticket links.
